On the scan, 15480-16150, v 0-150 is plain silk except the whips at 15455-15570, v 0-75 (no bank ink, no ripples). The two readings must meet at the frame's cross-key seam check: either S3's shore_n starts at S4b's (15500, 112, est) and runs off the silk's top edge (est) east of the willow, or S4b's far bank turns off the top edge at about u 15450-15500. lessons: Second pass: read every neighbour's `note` for things placed on your side of the seam. S4b's far-bank ground named a willow foot at (15520, 70), 20 px into S3, with no entity in either map; S3's merge had already flagged the same crown as 'recorded by nobody'. A point named in a neighbour's note is a missing entity on whichever side its main point falls.

Second pass: a rounded mass with no collar, neck or hair is not a back. Read the outline's widest part: a seated back is widest at the shoulders (its top), a basin or basket at its belly (its bottom). On S3 the 'diner seen from behind' was a basin under a heap of fruit or flowers; the restyle had invented a man there, as it invents diners all over that hall.

Second pass: contrast-stretched crops (sharp normalise 1-99 %) at zoom 2.5-3.5 read faint figures best; zoom 4-5 adds only the silk's weave, and plain crops at zoom 3 lose faint strokes. Put the tile restyle and, where it disagrees, the overview restyle beside the scan: when the three readings differ (figure, cloth, panel), record the thing at low with all three.
